newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's economic policy may be ready in a month.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's economic policy may be ready in a month.

text.p: Ecuador's newly appointed Finance Minister, Carlos Davalos, said on Thursday the country's economic policy might be ready in four weeks.
"This Friday, or on Monday, I will hold a press conference to announced the results of the evaluation, and, in four weeks, provide the president with a plan," Davalos told reporters.

"The situation is grim, but we want to confirm it first, in order to announce the details later. We have to correct the political practices that have led to this deplorable state, and we will make changes after reaching a consensus (on what needs to be done)," he said.
Davalos, a 69 year old lawyer-economist, was sworn in on Thursday afternoon as Finance Minister by newly appointed president Fabian Alarcon.
Alarcon, himself, was sworn in on Tuesday, after the impeachment of President Abdala Bucaram, who Congress ruled was mentally unfit to rule.
The new Ecuadoran authorities have said Bucaram has left the country's finances in a deplorable state, after months of unlimited spending.
Davalos said his first priority is to bring order to the country's public finances.
